name: Animal trypanosomiasis (nagana), carried by tsetse flies
_doc: challenge (0 to 1) is how strongly the vector pressures a tile: the product of the range conditions and the climate and vegetation envelope (sim/geography/content_rules.py). A host's loss in a year is annual_loss_at_full_challenge times the challenge. Hosts are herd animal ids (data/world/geography/resources/animals.json); an animal not listed is not a host.
range_note: The range box is the sub-Saharan distribution of Glossina; it also covers Madagascar and the Arabian south-west, which carry no tsetse, so those tiles are over-counted where wet enough. A species distribution is a biogeographic fact (dispersal), not a climate response, so it is data rather than derived.

range.source: Latitude: Wikipedia, Tsetse fly (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tsetse_fly, opened): 'tsetse flies were reported from a maximum latitude of approximately 15 north in Senegal (Niayes Region) to a minimum of 28.5 south in South Africa (KwaZulu-Natal Province)' (as of 1990), 'nearly 10,000,000 square kilometres in sub-Saharan Africa', 38 countries; the -29 to 15 box is that. FAO Connor (fao.org/4/t0599e/t0599e01.htm, opened) agrees: 'some 10 million km2 south of the Sahara'. The longitude span -18 to 52 is the continent's tsetse belt from Senegal to the Horn, not a separately sourced limit.

challenge_envelope.source: Temperature: PMC8648107 (opened): 'Tsetse flies thrive in areas with mean annual temperatures of 19-30 C', 'Temperatures below 19 C slow down tsetse activity', above 36 C 'survival capacity of close to zero'; the 20-30 optimum and 16-34 tolerated edges bracket that. Rainfall and forest edges: FAO (fao.org/4/y5342e/y5342e06.htm, opened) gives no mm limits, only a 'dry band' set at a Length of Growing Period of 170 days and species richness rising with luxuriant vegetation; the 900-3000 and 500-4500 mm edges and the forest fraction remain a stand-in of the right order.

hosts.cattle.source: FAO, Connor, Trypanosomiasis control (fao.org/4/t0599e/t0599e01.htm, opened), Mkwaja Ranch, Tanzania, a high-challenge site: 'none of the 18 untreated cattle survived' the 31 months, while 3 of 37 drug-treated cattle died. All untreated animals dead within 2.6 years means a yearly loss of at least about half the herd; 0.5 is the low end of that reading. Trypanotolerant breeds exist and are not modelled.

hosts.horse.source: FAO, Connor (fao.org/4/t0599e/t0599e01.htm, opened), Table 1: pathogenicity for horses is '+++' for T. brucei and '++' for T. congolense and T. vivax, so the horse is at least as susceptible as the cattle above (0.5 a year at full challenge). Wikivet (en.wikivet.net/Trypanosomosis_-_Donkey) says horses can only be maintained in tsetse-infested areas with trypanocidal drugs. 0.9 is a ballpark above the cattle figure, not a measured rate.
